notes.decision: ⲅⲣⲟ = 'prevail, conquer.' The clause is the chapter's thesis: the Darkness was conquered through the agency of the Five Greatnesses. Subject is implicit (the powers of light); ⲁⲣⲁⲩ 'over them' = over the dark powers.

Lycopolitan ⲩⲧⲟⲉ = ϥⲧⲟⲟⲩ 'four.' With the perfective ⲁ-, the clause means '(then) the four (remaining) Greatnesses were revealed' — narratively bridging from the unitary first Greatness (Father in silence) to the four manifest emanations enumerated in lines 19-31. The article ⲡ- before ⲩⲧⲟⲉ may be elided/absorbed; transcription shows 'ⲁ ⲩⲧⲟⲉ' with space.

'The Mother of Life, the Great Spirit' — both standard Manichaean titles applied here apparently to the same figure as the Second Greatness, paired with ⲁⲍⲁⲛ ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ 'beside the First Man.' The 'Great Spirit' apposition with the Mother is unusual in canonical schemata (where Living Spirit is masculine and a separate emanation), and the schema here groups the Mother+First Man+Five Sons together as the Second Greatness.

'The Great Builder' — ⲉⲕⲱⲧ = ⲕⲱⲧ 'builder, fashioner.' This is the Manichaean Great Architect (μέγας Δημιουργός), here grouped under the Third Greatness alongside the Beloved of the Lights and the Living Spirit with his Five Sons.

Note the ordinal mismatch with canonical Manichaean catalogues: here the Third Ambassador is the Fourth Greatness in the page's own counting. The 'Third' in his title is preserved as a fixed epithet (per accumulated vocabulary), even when the local enumeration places him in fourth position.
'Jesus the Radiance' — fixed translation per terminology guide. The Fifth Greatness, identified directly with Jesus and his powers/emanations.

'The whole Building' — the cosmic construction (the entire fashioned cosmos). The Five Sons of the First Man are connected with the whole Building, while the Five Sons of the Living Spirit are spread out as bearers in five places — referencing the Manichaean cosmological architecture where the Living Spirit's sons are the cosmic supports/bearers (Splenditenens, King of Glory, etc.).

Translated 'twelve ascendings' — ⲥⲛⲁⲩⲥⲉ = '12' (= ⲙⲛⲧⲥⲛⲟⲟⲩⲥⲉ); ⲧⲁⲗⲉ = 'ascend, mount.' Feminine ⲧ- article with collective force. The reference is probably to the twelve cosmic ascensions/emanations of light, to which the Call and Hearing are added as Father and Mother.

ⲧⲱⲍⲙⲉ here functions as the noun 'the Call' (Manichaean qrīā), not the verb 'summon forth' as in earlier vocabulary. Paired with the standard Manichaean ⲡⲥⲱⲧⲙⲉ 'the Hearing/Listening' (ʿānyā). Together these form the Father/Mother dyad mentioned in line 3.

Greek-form word of unclear identification — possibly ναύλοχοι 'those at harbor,' or a corruption of ἀνάδοχοι 'sponsors,' or another Greek loan. Left in the lacuna marker rather than guessed. Flagged for review.
ⲣ̄ⲁⲓⲍⲏⲧ = 'be downcast in heart, sorrow.' The clause describes the noble man's humbled state under his enemies' grasp. ⲑⲃ̄ⲓⲟ 'humbling, abasement' per terminology guide.
ⲕⲁⲣⲁⲓⲧϥ̄ = ⲕⲁⲣⲱϥ 'silence, stillness' — the captive's silent suffering. Lycopolitan ⲁⲓ for ⲱ.
ⲉⲩⲧⲉⲛⲏⲥ = Greek εὐγενής 'noble, well-born.' The figure is the noble offspring (ϣⲛ̄ⲏⲣⲉ) whose oppression by enemies is the parable for the First Man's capture.

ϣⲃ̄ⲓⲁⲓⲧ qualitative of ϣⲓⲃⲉ 'change, alter' — 'is altered/changed in comparison with that (likeness) of the First Man.' The Living Spirit's likeness differs from the First Man's because it descends as victor with a commandment, not as captive.

ⲧⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲛⲧ = 'liken, compare.' The Living Spirit is likened to a judge whom the King sends because of violence done to a noble man (the First Man). Standard Manichaean cosmological allegory: First Man as oppressed prince, Living Spirit as avenging judge-emissary.
= ⲡϫⲓⲛϭⲟⲛⲥ̄ 'the violence, the act of force' (cf. accumulated vocab ⲙⲛⲧⲝⲓⲛⲟⲁⲛⲥ̄). The judge is sent 'because of the violence' done to the noble man.

Tentatively rendered 'judiciousness' as a quality paired with righteousness in a judicial context. The Lyc. ⲝ corresponds to ϫ; the root may be ϫⲡⲓⲟ ('rebuke, accuse') giving 'judicious-rebuke, censorial uprightness,' or ϫⲱⲡⲉ in another sense. Confidence low; flagged for terminology review.

Translated 'wicked' (qualitative adjective). The form recurs in line 24 modifying 'his other [associates]' where a negative-moral sense fits. Etymology unclear — possibly a Lyc. reflex of a defilement-root. Confidence low. Alternative reading 'concerning her/it' (= ⲉⲧⲃⲏⲏⲧⲥ̄) is grammatically possible but contextually weak.

Tentatively 'destroying them' as a verb of violent action paired with ⲍⲁⲧⲃⲟⲩ 'killing them.' The form is unclear — possibly Lyc. for ϩⲏⲧ-ⲟⲩ ('cast/throw them down') or a related destruction-verb. Flagged for review.
Translated 'obey' as Lyc. reflex of ⲥⲱⲧⲙ̄ 'listen, hear, obey.' The negation ⲁⲛ in 'those who do not obey' fits the disciplinary context of the preceding judicial sequence.
Per accumulated vocabulary, ⲡⲱⲕ ⲛⲍⲏⲧ = 'intent/purpose of heart.' Here applied to the servants of the judge: 'they do the intent (= will) of their lord.'

Tentatively 'his other associates/companions' — ⲇⲁⲙ uncertain, possibly a noun for confederate/cohort, or possibly an abbreviation for a power-class (δαίμων > 'demons,' or δύναμις > 'powers'). The compound on line 26, ⲛ̄ⲇⲁⲙⲡⲛⲁⲃⲉ 'companions of Sin,' supports a 'companion/associate' reading.

Translated 'companions of Sin.' The construction ⲛ̄-ⲇⲁⲙ-ⲡⲛⲁⲃⲉ where ⲇⲁⲙ functions as 'fellow, associate' yields 'fellow-sinners, accomplices in sin' — the archons who collaborated with the King of Darkness in the assault on the First Man. Capitalized 'Sin' per terminology guide for cosmic principle.

ⲙⲛⲧ-ⲟⲩⲁ-ϩⲏⲧ = 'state of single-heartedness' = 'single-mindedness, audacity, defiance.' Paired here antithetically with ⲡⲉϩⲑⲃ̄ⲓ̈ⲟ 'his abasement': the judge measures each one according to (1) the boldness of his transgression and (2) the resulting humiliation. Rendered 'single-mindedness' to preserve the etymological one-heartedness.

Tentatively 'he scourged/afflicted them backward.' ⲉϣⲧ likely from a root meaning 'afflict, torment, scourge'; ⲥⲁⲭⲱⲩ likely Lyc. ⲥⲁⲡⲁϩⲟⲩ 'behind, backward.' Possibly the Manichaean image of binding the archons facing-away from the realm of light.
Translated 'seated below.' ϩⲙⲉⲥⲧ is the Lyc. qualitative of ϩⲙⲟⲟⲥ 'sit, dwell' + ⲁⲡⲓⲧⲛ̄ 'downward.' Spatial-cosmological idiom for the lower-placed archons.
Translated 'being squeezed' as qualitative of reduplicated ϩⲱϫϩⲱϫ 'press, oppress, constrain.' Fits the bond-imagery (ⲙⲡ̄ⲣⲉ ⲉⲥⲛⲁϣⲧ 'strong bond').
Translated 'desire of heart.' ϣⲱⲕ ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ = 'pleasure/desire of heart' — the will-direction of the archonic powers operating downward.
'Father of Life' — Manichaean cosmological title; here likely the Father of Greatness (Father of the Living) in his role of establishing the hidden cosmic structure.
'One who hides' — ⲣⲉϥ- ('one who does') + ⲧϩⲉⲡⲧ (causative of ϩⲏⲡ 'hide'). Forms an agent-noun parallel to ⲣⲉϩ†ⲥⲃⲱ 'teacher.'
Translated '[gave] him kingship.' Uses the established idiom ϯ ⲡⲟⲣⲟ 'give kingship/establish as king' from the glossary; ⲛⲉϩ = Lyc. 'to him' (= ⲛⲁϥ).

Translated 'the establishment that was lacking.' ϣⲱϩⲧ = 'be wanting, deficient.' Fits Manichaean theology: the King of Darkness's kingship is established only on a defective register, contrasted with First Man's true kingship.
Tentatively 'bond of agreement.' ⲧⲟⲁⲧ uncertain — possibly Lyc. variant of ⲧⲱⲧ 'agreement, persuasion' (cf. ⲡⲓⲧⲱⲧ in vocab). Could alternatively reflect a possessive 'her bond.'
Read as ⲛ̄(ⲥⲉ)ϩⲱⲝⲛⲉ = 'and they fail/cease' (= ⲱⲝⲛⲉ from glossary). Eschatological: the cosmic structures fail in the Great Fire.
Translated 'and they will rescue him forth.' Read as ⲛ̄ⲥⲉⲛⲁⲍⲙϥ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ (assimilation of ⲙ) — ⲛⲁⲍⲙⲉϩ from vocab = 'save, rescue.' Refers to the rescue of light from the dissolving cosmos.
Translated 'too is shut up.' ϩⲱϩ = emphatic 'also/too' (Lyc. ϩⲱⲱϥ). ⲟϣ likely from ⲱϣ 'bind, fasten, shut up' — paralleling 'in the bond and the chain.'

Translated tentatively 'the prison(?).' Lexeme uncertain. Possibly = ⲧⲍⲱⲛⲏ 'the Zone/Girdle' (Greek ζώνη — see vocab) with ϩ/ⲍ alternation, fitting the Manichaean cosmology where captured archons are bound in the zodiacal zone after the Third Ambassador's coming. Alternative: a Coptic term for 'fastness/enclosure.' Flagged for further investigation.
Translated 'those taken (in).' Past relative + ⲱⲡ/ⲧⲱⲡ 'gather, take in.' These are the captured archonic powers awaiting inspection — fits the simile of the king inspecting his prisoners/works.

Translated 'chiefs.' Compound: ⲣⲉϥ- ('one who does') + ⲣ̄- ('do/make') + ⲁⲡⲉ ('head') = 'head-doer' = chief/foreman. Parallels ⲣⲉϩ†ⲥⲃⲱ 'teacher.' Fits the inspection-of-craftsmen simile: foremen reporting to the king.

Translated tentatively 'they have given life to.' Reading ⲁⲩ-ⲭⲱⲛϩ where ⲭⲱⲛϩ = ⲱⲛϩ̄/ⲁⲛϩ 'live, give life.' The artisan giving life to his works fits the simile. Alternative: 'they have completed/laid out' (cognate with ⲕⲱⲛϩ 'complete'). Confidence moderate.
Translated 'arrays.' Greek loanword παρεμβολαί 'encampments, arrays, formations' — what the king inspects alongside the works. Standard military-administrative term.
Translated 'when he came forth.' ⲛ̄ⲧⲁⲣⲉ-ϩ-ⲉⲓ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ — temporal + 3sg.m + 'come' + 'forth.' The forth-coming of the Third Ambassador to inspect the cosmos.
Translated 'spread forth.' ⲥⲏⲣ qualitative of ⲥⲱⲣ 'scatter, spread, disperse' + ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'out, forth.' Paired with ⲉⲩⲥⲙⲁⲛⲧ 'established' — the works are both established and spread out.

Translated 'host' provisionally. Lexeme is unattested in standard Coptic dictionaries; possibilities include (a) Greek χορός 'troop, choral host' (with unusual ⲍ for χ), (b) a Lyc. noun related to ⲥⲱⲣ 'spread, scatter' (cf. immediately following ⲉⲩⲥⲛⲣ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'spread out'), or (c) ϩⲱⲣ 'guardian.' Context ('the X of the archons being spread out, established among them, in upper/lower/outer/inner sides') requires a dispersive collective.
Read as Greek παράπτωμα + Coptic ⲗⲁⲩⲉ 'any' = 'any transgression,' with the construction ⲉⲙⲁⲍⲧⲉ ⲛ̄ + negative-particle 'holding back from any transgression.' Note Lyc. spelling ⲡⲁⲣⲁⲙⲡⲧⲟ for παραπτω-.

Translated 'the matter' provisionally. May be Lyc. ϩⲏⲡ 'hidden thing, secret' or ϩⲱⲡ 'judgment'; reduplicated ⲡⲡ unclear. The relative clause ⲉⲧⲁⲕ- 'which you (sg.)...' indicates an object the Living Spirit has done/uttered.

Translated 'they were gathered.' Verb unattested in standard Coptic; paired with ⲁⲩⲭⲉⲥⲧⲟⲩ ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ 'they were conveyed upward,' so a verb of gathering/binding/seizing fits. Possibly related to ⲕⲱⲙ̄ⲧ̄ 'gather' or a metathesis of ⲕⲙ̄ⲕⲙ̄ 'be silent.'

Translated 'furnace' on contextual grounds (paired with ⲣⲱⲭⲍ̄ 'burning' and ⲧⲥⲉⲧⲉ 'fire'). The lexeme is unattested; could possibly be a metallurgical implement or smelting vessel. Pictures the pre-cosmic refinement/binding of dark powers.
Read as ⲥⲁⲧⲉ 'shoot forth, sprout' with negative final clause: 'so that they might not put forth (shoots).' Fits agricultural register of bitter trees not putting forth bitter fruit (line 25).

Translated 'planted/plantings.' ⲧⲱⲟ̄ⲉ here = ⲧⲱϭⲉ 'plant, set in.' The verbal use 'they planted' and the cognate noun 'their plantings' both follow standard Manichaean agricultural-soteriological register (cf. ⲡⲱϩⲛ 'planting' in accumulated vocab).
Standard Lycopolitan abbreviation/contraction of ⲡⲡⲣⲓ̈ⲉ 'the Radiance' (accumulated vocab). Active verbal sense preserved.

Translated 'expelled them forth' from ⲃⲱⲧⲉ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'drive out, expel' (Lyc ⲁ for ⲱ). The verb in this triplet (expel / bind / afflict) is judicial-punitive, fitting the broader narrative of binding the dark powers in the Girdle.
Reduplicated form of ϩⲱϣⲙ̄ 'afflict, oppress' with 3pl suffix. Translated 'afflicted them.' Could also be from ϩⲟϣϩⲱϣ 'crush'; sense is the same — punishment of bound powers.
ⲣⲱⲭⲉ̂ = Lyc ⲣⲱⲕϩ 'burn'; ⲛ̄ⲥ-ⲧⲉⲕⲟ = infinitive of ⲧⲁⲕⲟ 'destroy.' Translated 'burn and destroy.' Distinguished from ⲣ̄ⲱⲭϩ̄ 'consume' (eschatological fire term in glossary).

Translated 'fragrant-breath' from ⲡⲱϣⲙ 'breath, exhalation' + ⲛⲟⲩϥⲉ 'fragrance, sweet odor.' In Manichaean cosmology the soul/spirit's fragrant exhalation is technical. Alternative reading 'incense-worship' (= ϣⲙ̄ϣⲉ-ⲛⲟⲩϥⲉ) is possible but less likely given the noun-stem ⲡⲱϣⲙ.
ⲕⲁⲣⲁⲓⲧϥ̄ = ⲕⲁⲣⲱⲱⲩ + suffix 'silence, stillness.' Translated 'silence' both here and at line 29.
Lyc reflex of ⲛⲉϩⲥⲉ 'awaken.' Eschatological awakening at the time of the end.

Translated as 'destruction' from Greek ἀναίρεσις 'killing, taking-away, destruction.' The two spellings (with and without -ⲡ-) are scribal variants of the same word. Refers to the eschatological cosmic dissolution. Alternative reading ἀνάπαυσις 'rest' is grammatically possible but contextually inferior — the passage describes the Father scattering forth defilement and gathering light alone, which is destructive-purgative, not restful.
Translated 'encompassing' from ⲕⲱⲛⲥ̄ / ⲕⲱⲛⲧ̄ 'wrap around, embrace, surround.' The First Man encompasses the totality even as he scatters out the foreign defilement.
Translated 'rising-up' from ⲧⲱⲟⲩⲛ 'rise.' The technical complement to ⲧⲟⲩⲱ 'raise' — here the intransitive nominalized form for the upward motion of light gathered out of all things.
Translated 'this great agony' from ⲁⲣⲱⲛ = Greek ἀγών 'contest, struggle, ordeal.' Standard Manichaean term for the cosmic combat. Lyc ⲣⲱ for ⲅⲱ.

Translated 'there have come to pass the dissolution and the formation' — taking ⲁⲩϩⲉ as past 3pl of ϩⲉ 'fall, happen' with the doublet 'dissolution / formation' as logical subjects. ⲡⲟⲩⲱⲑ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ = 'wiping-out, dissolution' (ⲟⲩⲱⲧⲃ̄ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ). ⲡⲙⲟⲩⲛⲕ̄ = 'formation, fashioning' — the Manichaean cosmic Image/Statue assembled at the end.

Translated 'hot-stone' tentatively. Etymology unclear; possibly related to ⲱⲃϣ̄/ⲱⲃⲣ ('white-hot iron' or 'glowing implement'), or a specialized term for the heated object dropped into milk to ripen/cook it. The ancient cooking technique of plunging hot stones or irons into milk to thicken/cook it fits perfectly. Flag for review.

ⲥⲟⲩⲱⲧϩ = ⲥⲱⲧϩ 'extract, draw forth, refine.' ⲥⲟⲩⲱϣⲙ̄ⲉ = ⲱϣⲙ̄ 'quench, extinguish.' Together they describe the hot stone's double action in milk: drawing out moisture/essence and quenching its own heat. Standard physical-process pairing.
Greek loanword πέσσειν 'cook, ripen, digest.' The hot stone ripens/cooks the milk. Translated 'ripens.'

Three substances of the maternal cosmic gathering: oil, sweetness/fatness, and beauty of milk. ⲕⲛⲓⲉ = Sah. ⲕⲛⲛⲉ 'fatness, sweetness.' These are the nourishing substances by which the Mother-figure draws the captive light back into herself.

Standard Manichaean cosmological pair Call/Answer (Ruf/Antwort) per accumulated vocabulary. The whole sequence here identifies the enthumesis = counsel of life = Call+Answer addressed to the elements.
Standard Lycopolitan idiom 'stand fast on his feet' (vocab: ⲧⲏⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗). Here 3sg.m subject — the eschatological standing of the Awakened.
